Evidence · Standards

Standards we follow

We follow public drafts and published specifications for liquid cooling and the standards for metering boundaries, so that the acceptance criteria we use stay aligned with industry standards.

What we follow

Open Compute Project, Cooling Environments. We follow the liquid-cooling workstream's public drafts and published specifications, with a focus on commissioning evidence, coolant quality and the boundaries between rack, CDU and facility. The interfaces are being specified: in 2026 Google contributed its Project Deschutes CDU specification to OCP, and quick-disconnect suppliers have asked for the 2019 cold-plate requirements to be updated. In the public documents we have read, we have not found a complete requirement for what a turnover package must contain; that is the gap our turnover package addresses. The documents we have read include the Modular Technology Cooling System for Cloud Scale (Rev 1, August 2025), the Open Rack V3 Blind Mate Manifold Specification (Rev 1.0) and the public-review draft of Thermal Boundaries in AI Infrastructure (v0.98, 2026).

Energy-reuse metrics. The metrics that make heat reuse auditable already exist: the Energy Reuse Factor (ERF) as defined in ISO/IEC 30134-6 and EN 50600-4-6, the Energy Reuse Effectiveness (ERE) published by The Green Grid as a companion to PUE, and the metering-boundary requirement in Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364 for larger EU data centres. We use them in our own reporting, and we recommend them wherever PUE is still the only number on the slide.

Public writing. The three-clock model, the ten leak points and the metering-boundary argument were all published first as open articles and posts, and revised in public with input from operators, water-chemistry specialists and insurers. The versions on this site are current and are revised as the industry discussion moves.

What we look for in a specification

  • Every performance requirement names the load level, temperature and boundary it applies at.
  • Every pressure boundary has a test, an acceptance criterion and a record owner.
  • Cleanliness and passivation are treated as separate requirements with separate evidence.
  • Heat reuse is measured at the hand-off boundary, not estimated from the IT load.

Questions this page answers

Which standards apply to liquid-cooling heat reuse and metering?

The Energy Reuse Factor (ERF) in ISO/IEC 30134-6 and EN 50600-4-6, the Energy Reuse Effectiveness (ERE) from The Green Grid, and the metering-boundary requirement in Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364 for EU data centres with at least 500 kW installed IT demand. For the thermal environment itself, ASHRAE's W-classes give the facility-water temperature envelopes. Return-water grade →

Is there an open specification for liquid-cooling commissioning evidence?

Not in the public documents we have read. The Open Compute Project's Cooling Environments workstream publishes drafts on rack, CDU and facility interfaces and white papers on liquid-cooling integration, and has received Google's Project Deschutes CDU specification (v1.0 released February 2026), but none of the public documents we have read fully specifies what a turnover package must contain. The record structure this site uses, three questions for each of ten leak points, supplements them; applicable standards, OEM documents and the project's acceptance criteria govern. The turnover package →
